extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, submitting, correcting, and handling patent drawings, annotated sheets, replacement drawings, models/exhibits/specimens, and electronic sequence/program listings during U.S. patent prosecution, including new-matter rules and timing requirements. Covers examiner and Office procedures for acceptance, rejection, return, and disposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant responsibility for drawing changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States Patent and Trademark Office does not make drawing changes. It is applicant’s responsibility to ensure that the drawings are corrected. Corrections must be made in accordance with the instructions below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 6.39 whenever the applicant has filed a request for the Office to make drawing changes; follow with form paragraph 6.40. The Office may notify applicant of required corrections; applicant must effect corrections as instructed to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement drawing sheets labeling and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date of an application must be labeled in the top margin as either 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet' pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121(d). A replacement sheet must include all of the figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet, even if only one figure is being amended. The figure or figure number of the amended drawing(s) must not be labeled as 'amended.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An explanation of the changes made must be presented either in the drawing amendments section or remarks section of the amendment paper. If changes are not accepted, applicant will be notified of required corrective action in the next Office action. See 37 CFR 1.84 and 1.121(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotated drawing sheets requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A marked-up copy of any amended drawing figure, including annotations indicating the changes made, may be submitted or required by the examiner. The annotated drawing sheets must be clearly labeled as 'Annotated Sheet' and must be presented in the amendment or remarks section that explains the change(s) to the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotated sheets filed by an applicant and used for correction of the drawing will not be returned. All such annotated sheets must be in ink or permanent prints. If a canceled figure is reinstated, add a brief description of the view to the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of drawing corrections and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is required to submit acceptable corrected drawings within the time period set in the Office action. Failure to take corrective action within the set period will result in ABANDONMENT of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If corrected drawings are required in a Notice of Allowability (PTOL-37), the new drawings MUST be filed within the THREE MONTH shortened statutory period set for reply in the 'Notice of Allowability.' Extensions of time may NOT be obtained under 37 CFR 1.136 for filing corrected drawings after mailing of a Notice of Allowability. See 37 CFR 1.85(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying indicia on drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying indicia, if provided, should include the title of the invention, inventor’s name, and application number, or docket number (if any) if an application number has not been assigned to the application. If this information is provided, it must be placed on the front of each sheet and within the top margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps Office identify sheets; place information consistently in top margin/front of each sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of canceled figures
rubrics_metrics.description: A canceled figure may be reinstated. An amendment should be made to the specification adding the brief description of the view if a canceled figure is reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a drawing figure is canceled, a replacement sheet must be submitted without the figure; if the canceled figure was the only drawing on the sheet, a marked-up annotated copy showing cancellation may suffice. Amend brief description of the drawings accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner notification and explanation when corrections not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the corrected or changed drawing is not accepted, for example, because the submitted corrections or changes are erroneous, involve new matter, or do not include all necessary corrections, the applicant will be notified and informed of any required corrective action in the next Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should explicitly and clearly set forth all the reasons for not approving the corrections to the drawings in the next communication to the applicant. See MPEP § 608.02(p) for suggested form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing corrections that may be made without applicant's annotated sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application is ready for issue except for a slight defect in the drawing not involving change in structure, the examiner will prepare a letter indicating the change to be made and may include a marked-up copy; certain slight corrections may be suggested without requiring annotated sheets from the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative acceptable corrections without annotated sheets include: (A) adding two or three reference characters or exponents; (B) changing one or two numerals or figure ordinals; (C) removing superfluous matter; (D) adding or reversing directional arrows; (E) changing Roman numerals to Arabic numerals to agree with specification; (F) adding section lines or brackets where easily executed; (G) changing lead lines; (H) correcting misspelled legends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings will not be returned
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings will not be returned to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotated sheets filed for correction will not be returned either. If drawings are to be returned, specific provisions apply (see 37 CFR 1.94 for models/exhibits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable applications and handling of informal drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the drawings submitted in an application have been indicated by the applicant as 'informal,' but the drawings are considered acceptable by OPAP, the examiner should not require replacement of the drawings. In IFW applications, generally, the most recently filed drawings will be used for printing, unless they have been indicated as 'Not Entered.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner makes an objection to the drawings, require correction in reply to the Office action that sets forth the objection. For allowed applications, form PTOL-37 provides a checkbox for requiring corrected drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement drawings received after Notice of Allowability (utility applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where replacement drawings are received in utility patent applications after the Notice of Allowability was mailed, the replacement drawings are handled by the Office of Data Management. Submission to the examiner is not necessary unless an amendment to the specification accompanies the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is applicant’s responsibility to see that no new matter is added when submitting replacement drawings after allowance because they will not normally be reviewed by an examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models, exhibits, specimens admission conditions (37 CFR 1.91)
rubrics_metrics.description: A model or exhibit will not be admitted as part of the record of an application unless it: (1) substantially conforms to the requirements of § 1.52 or § 1.84; (2) is specifically required by the Office; or (3) is filed with a petition under this section including the fee set forth in § 1.17(h) and an explanation of why entry of the model or exhibit in the file record is necessary to demonstrate patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not substantially conforming under paragraph (a)(1), the model must be accompanied by photographs showing multiple views of the material features that conform to § 1.84. A video/DVD submission must be accompanied by photographs of the content depicted, not a photograph of the storage medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models and exhibits generally not required to demonstrate operability
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of cases involving perpetual motion, a model is not ordinarily required by the Office to demonstrate the operability of a device. If operability is questioned, the applicant must establish it to the satisfaction of the examiner, but may choose his or her own way of doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may require a model or physical exhibit if deemed necessary for any purpose in examination. Models/exhibits required or submitted under petition must be accompanied by photographs that substantially conform to § 1.84, showing the material features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling, labeling, and storage of models/exhibits/specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: All models and exhibits received in the USPTO should be taken to the Technology Center assigned the related application for examination. The receipt of all models and exhibits to be entered into the application file must be properly recorded on an artifact sheet. A label indicating the application number, filing date, and attorney’s name and address should be attached to the model or exhibit so that it is clearly identified and easily returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the model or exhibit cannot be conveniently stored in an artifact folder, it should not be accepted. Models/exhibits may be used during interviews and should be removed by applicant at the conclusion. Any model left with the examiner that is not made part of the application may be disposed of at the Office’s discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return and disposal of models/exhibits/specimens (37 CFR 1.94)
rubrics_metrics.description: Models, exhibits, or specimens may be returned to the applicant if no longer necessary for the conduct of business before the Office. When applicant is notified that an item is no longer necessary and will be returned, applicant must arrange for the return at the applicant’s expense. The Office will dispose of perishables without notice unless applicant notifies the Office upon submission that a return is desired and makes arrangements promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is responsible for retaining the actual model/exhibit/specimen for the enforceable life of any patent resulting from the application, except where (A) the model/exhibit conforms to § 1.52 or 1.84; (B) has been described by photographs conforming to § 1.84; or (C) is perishable. Notification will set a time period (normally two months) to arrange return; extensions under § 1.136 are available except for perishables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph for notifying return arrangements required (6.48)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 6.48: The [1] is no longer necessary for the conduct of business before the Office. Applicant must arrange for the return of the model, exhibit or specimen at the applicant’s expense in accordance with 37 CFR 1.94(a). Applicant is given TWO MONTHS from the mailing date of this letter to make arrangements for return to avoid disposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include bracketed identification of the item no longer needed; note perishables may be disposed without notice. For plant specimens see MPEP § 1607 and 37 CFR 1.166.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter: prohibition and examiner actions
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment shall introduce new matter into the disclosure of the invention (35 U.S.C. 132). When new matter is introduced into the specification, the amendment should be objected to under 35 U.S.C. 132 (35 U.S.C. 251 if reissue) and a requirement made to cancel the new matter. The subject matter considered new must be clearly identified by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the new matter has been entered into the claims or affects their scope, the claims affected should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph. The examiner’s holding of new matter may be petitionable or appealable (see MPEP § 608.04(c)). Use form paragraph 7.28 to object to new matter in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: New matter examples and scope guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: New matter includes addition of wholly unsupported subject matter, adding specific percentages or compounds after a broader original disclosure, or omission of a step from a method. Matter not present on the filing date that is added after filing is usually new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Wertheim and MPEP §§ 2163.05–2163.07 for guidance in determining whether added characteristics are inherent and hence not new matter. If subject matter capable of illustration is originally claimed but not shown in the drawing, the applicant is required to add it to the drawing (see MPEP § 608.01(l)). Replacement drawings containing new matter should not be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendments and original disclosure status
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment present on the filing date of the application (e.g., filed along with the filing of the application) is considered a part of the original disclosure. A preliminary amendment filed after the filing date is not part of the original disclosure of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on or after Sept. 21, 2004, the Office will automatically treat any preliminary amendment under 37 CFR 1.115(a)(1) present on the filing date as part of the original disclosure. Applicants are encouraged to avoid submitting preliminary amendments to reduce processing burden and delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewability of examiner’s holding of new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the new matter is confined to amendments to the specification, review of the examiner’s requirement for cancellation is by way of petition. But where the alleged new matter is introduced into or affects the claims, thus necessitating their rejection on this ground, the question is appealable and should not be considered on petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2163.06. If new matter affects claims, make a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) using form paragraph 7.31.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing/table/computer program listing on compact disc requirements (37 CFR 1.52 & 1.77)
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic compact discs must conform to ISO 9660 and contents must be in ASCII. A compact disc must be enclosed in a hard case within an unsealed padded mailing envelope and accompanied by a transmittal letter on paper listing machine format, operating system compatibility, list of files with names, sizes, and creation dates, and any other special information necessary to identify and interpret the information on the disc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any compact disc must be submitted in duplicate unless it contains only the Sequence Listing required by § 1.821(e). The transmittal letter must state that the two discs are identical. Replacement discs must be submitted as replacement copies with labeling 'COPY 1 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY' and 'COPY 2 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY.' Compact discs submitted will not be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference and fee/size considerations for electronic listings
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must contain an incorporation-by-reference of the material on the compact disc in a separate paragraph (§ 1.77(b)(5)), identifying each compact disc by the names of the files, their date of creation and sizes in bytes. Any sequence listing in compliance with § 1.821(c) or (e), and any computer program listing filed in an electronic medium in compliance with §§ 1.52(e) and 1.96, will be excluded when determining the application size fee if the listing is submitted in ASCII text as part of an associated file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may require applicant to amend the specification to include on paper any part of the specification previously submitted on compact disc. For purposes of application size fee, three kilobytes of content submitted on an electronic medium other than the Office electronic filing system shall be counted as a sheet of paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unreadable or noncompliant files on compact disc
rubrics_metrics.description: If a file is unreadable on both copies of the disc, the unreadable file will be treated as not having been submitted. A file is unreadable if, for example, it is of a format that does not comply with the ISO/ASCII requirements, is corrupted by a computer virus, or is written onto a defective compact disc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label multiple discs to indicate order (e.g., '1 of X'). If multiple discs are submitted, the label shall indicate their order. Provide creation date on each disc and indicate Copy 1 or Copy 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement and order of application elements (37 CFR 1.77)
rubrics_metrics.description: The elements of the application, if applicable, should appear in the following order: (1) Utility application transmittal form; (2) Fee transmittal form; (3) Application data sheet; (4) Specification; (5) Drawings; (6) The inventor’s oath or declaration. The specification should include Title, Cross-reference to related applications, Statement regarding federally sponsored research, Names of parties to a joint research agreement, Reference to Sequence Listing/table/program listing on compact disc, Statement regarding prior disclosures, Background, Brief summary, Brief description of the drawings, Detailed description, Claims, Abstract, and Sequence Listing if on paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text of specification sections should be preceded by a section heading in uppercase without underlining or bold type. See 37 CFR 1.77(b) and (c) for section order and formatting.
